minutes.headline: Committee voted to make the town clerk an appointed position and approved the draft charter for public hearing.
minutes.summary: The Charter Review Committee reviewed survey results, then voted on keeping open town meeting, two regular town meetings a year, renaming the board of selectmen, an appointed town clerk, and term limits. The town clerk change drew the longest debate, with some members fearing it could sink the charter. The committee approved the draft charter and planned a public hearing for April 5. Public comment at the end raised the write-in vote minimum.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to make the town clerk an appointed position in the draft charter, after the longest debate of the meeting.
The committee approved the charter draft as the plan to move forward.
The committee voted to keep open town meeting, hold two regular town meetings a year, and rename the Board of Selectmen the Select Board.
The committee voted not to support term limits.
A resident asked the committee to reconsider a minimum vote for write-in winners; members voted by show of hands to put it on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: If the charter reaches Town Meeting, residents would be asked to vote on whether the clerk, now an office residents may elect, becomes a position filled by appointment, along with the other changes in the draft.
watch_next: A public hearing on the draft charter is planned for Thursday, April 5.
The final draft is due out by Sunday the 18th; the next meeting is March 28, and the write-in minimum vote question is on that agenda.
